dmm-2012-tiebreaker-01.title: Parametrize the fold
dmm-2012-tiebreaker-01.body:
Place the sheet as $[0,8]\times[0,11]$ with the top-left corner $A=(0,11)$. Let the corner land on the right edge at $X=(8,11-t)$, $0\le t\le11$. The fold (crease) is the perpendicular bisector of $AX$: it passes through $M=(4,11-\frac t2)$ with direction $(t,8)$ (perpendicular to $AX=(8,-t)$). Points of the crease inside the sheet are $(4+\lambda t,\ 11-\frac t2+8\lambda)$ with
$$|\lambda|\le\frac4t\ \ (0\le x\le8),\qquad -\frac{11-t/2}8\le\lambda\le\frac t{16}\ \ (0\le y\le11).$$
The crease length is $\sqrt{t^2+64}\,(\lambda_{\max}-\lambda_{\min})$, with $\lambda_{\max}=\min(\frac4t,\frac t{16})$ and $\lambda_{\min}=-\min(\frac4t,\frac{11-t/2}8)$. Three ranges:

* $0<t\le11-\sqrt{57}\approx3.45$: $\lambda_{\max}-\lambda_{\min}=\frac t{16}+\frac{11-t/2}8=\frac{11}8$, length $\frac{11}8\sqrt{t^2+64}\ge11$ (the crease runs from the top to the bottom edge, shortest when $t\to0$).
* $11-\sqrt{57}\le t\le8$: $\lambda_{\max}-\lambda_{\min}=\frac t{16}+\frac4t=\frac{t^2+64}{16t}$, length $\frac{(t^2+64)^{3/2}}{16t}$, minimized where $3t^2=t^2+64$, i.e. $t=4\sqrt2$, with value $\frac{96^{3/2}}{16\cdot4\sqrt2}=6\sqrt3\approx10.39$.
* $8\le t\le11$: $\lambda_{\max}-\lambda_{\min}=\frac8t$, length $\frac{8\sqrt{t^2+64}}{t}=8\sqrt{1+\frac{64}{t^2}}$, decreasing in $t$, smallest at $t=11$: $\frac{8\sqrt{185}}{11}\approx9.89$.

Comparing $11$, $6\sqrt3\approx10.39$ and $\frac{8\sqrt{185}}{11}\approx9.89$, the minimum is $\frac{8\sqrt{185}}{11}$ inches (corner folded to the bottom-right corner).

**Answer: $\dfrac{8\sqrt{185}}{11}$ inches**

dmm-2012-tiebreaker-02.title: Cut off three corner triangles
dmm-2012-tiebreaker-02.body:
The hexagon is the triangle $ABC$ minus the three corner triangles $ADI$, $BFE$, $CHG$. Let $u=AD$, $v=BF$, $w=CH$, each in $[0,4]$. Then $AI=4-w$, $BE=4-u$, $CG=4-v$, and since each corner has angle $60^\circ$,
$$[ADI]+[BFE]+[CHG]=\frac{\sqrt3}4\big[u(4-w)+v(4-u)+w(4-v)\big]=\frac{\sqrt3}4f(u,v,w).$$
$f\ge0$ with $f=0$ at $u=v=w=0$, so the largest hexagon is the whole triangle: $A_1=[ABC]=9\sqrt3$.

$f$ is linear in each variable separately, so its maximum over the cube $[0,4]^3$ occurs at a vertex. At the vertices $u,v,w\in\{0,4\}$: $f=0$ if all equal, and $f=16$ in all other cases (e.g. $f(4,0,0)=4\cdot4=16$, $f(4,4,0)=16+0+0=16$). So $f\le16$ and $A_2=9\sqrt3-\frac{\sqrt3}4\cdot16=5\sqrt3$.

Therefore $A_1-A_2=9\sqrt3-5\sqrt3=4\sqrt3$.

**Answer: $4\sqrt3$**
